findings.title: Arch Linux AUR 'Atomic Arch' Mass-Compromise Scope Expansion 400 → 1,500+ Packages; AUR Account Registrations Suspended 2026-06-16; Attackers Expanded From NPM-Stage Into Bun Installation Paths
findings.affected_technology: Arch Linux Arch User Repository (AUR) — abandoned-package hijacks plus entirely new malicious packages. Watchtower 2026-06-13 News covered the 400+ package campaign delivering a Rust credential-stealer + eBPF kernel rootkit via the 'atomic-lockfile' NPM stage. Material updates 2026-06-16: scope expanded to ≥1,500 packages (SW + BC 2026-06-16); attackers expanded distribution to Bun-based installation paths in addition to NPM 2026-06-12; Arch Linux suspended new AUR account registrations 2026-06-16 while cleanup continues. Sonatype + StepSecurity confirm any host that ran a tainted install must be treated as fully untrusted — eBPF-based hiding primitives make conventional endpoint scans insufficient; rebuild from clean media + rotate every ambient SSH key / browser cookie / Vault token / cloud session. Threat score stays at 8 — severity unchanged, scope materially expanded. Continues the broader 2026 developer-supply-chain cluster (Shai-Hulud / Miasma / IronWorm) but distinct in eBPF rootkit payload and package-ecosystem targeting.
findings.summary: Arch Linux AUR 'Atomic Arch' campaign expanded 400→1,500+ malicious packages, attackers added Bun installation paths, Arch suspended new account registrations 2026-06-16; eBPF rootkit means tainted hosts require rebuild not cleanup — inventory every Arch host that ran AUR installs since 2026-06-07, treat as compromised, rotate all ambient credentials.

findings.title: LiteSpeed cPanel CVE-2026-54420 Added To CISA KEV With BOD 26-04 Three-Day Federal Remediation Deadline; Second Invocation Of The 3-Day Window After Ivanti Sentry CVE-2026-10520
findings.affected_technology: LiteSpeed cPanel user-end plugin on cPanel/WHM shared-hosting platforms. Watchtower 2026-06-15 News at score 7 covered symlink-following privilege-escalation-to-root from any FTP / web-shell foothold. Material change 2026-06-16: CISA added CVE-2026-54420 to the KEV catalog with the BOD 26-04 three-day federal-agency remediation timer (BleepingComputer 2026-06-16). This is the second BOD 26-04 three-day timer invocation after Ivanti Sentry CVE-2026-10520 on 2026-06-11 — CISA reserves it for cases where compensating controls are weak and exploitation is straightforward. Effective industry deadline: 2026-06-19. Patch is the 2026-06-09 LiteSpeed plugin fix-version. Where the LiteSpeed plugin is not in use on a cPanel host, uninstall it entirely. Score raised to 8 on KEV addition + BOD 26-04 three-day timer.
findings.summary: LiteSpeed cPanel CVE-2026-54420 (CVSS 8.5) added to CISA KEV with BOD 26-04 three-day federal deadline (BC 2026-06-16) — second 3-day invocation after Ivanti Sentry CVE-2026-10520; effective industry deadline 2026-06-19; inventory cPanel/WHM hosts, patch to 2026-06-09 fix-version or uninstall the plugin if unused.

findings.title: Fortinet FortiSandbox CVE-2026-25089 + Sibling CVE-2026-39813 + CVE-2026-39808 Now Confirmed Under Active In-The-Wild Exploitation Per Defused Threat Intel; Was PoC-Only In 2026-06-11 News
findings.affected_technology: Fortinet FortiSandbox advanced threat-detection appliance (appliance + VM form factors). Watchtower 2026-06-11 News covered CVE-2026-25089 (pre-auth OS command injection via 'Start' parameter, CVSS 9.1) at score 7. Material change 2026-06-16: Defused threat-intel firm observed active in-the-wild exploitation of all three FortiSandbox CVEs within the prior 24 hours (BleepingComputer + TheHackerNews 2026-06-16). Sibling CVE-2026-39813 and CVE-2026-39808 are also being exploited; patches landed 2026-04-14, so the unpatched-exploitation window is now two months wide. All three are low-complexity command-injection-class issues, no user interaction. FortiSandbox by design ingests attacker-controlled artefacts — pre-auth RCE on the detonation appliance is a pre-auth RCE on the inspection plane, both a blind spot and a high-value pivot. Score raised to 8 on confirmed ITW exploitation across the three-CVE batch.
findings.summary: FortiSandbox CVE-2026-25089 + CVE-2026-39813 + CVE-2026-39808 confirmed under active ITW exploitation by Defused threat intel 2026-06-16 (was PoC-only 2026-06-11); patches available since 2026-04-14 — inventory FortiSandbox fleet, verify on 2026-04-14 fix-train, forensic-image + rebuild any unit not patched by mid-April, net-isolate management interfaces.

findings.title: JetBrains Marketplace — 15+ Malicious Plugins Designed To Steal Anthropic / OpenAI / Google AI API Keys From Developer IDEs; Second 2026 AI-Credential-Theft Cluster Targeting Developer-IDE Marketplace Surfaces After Mini Shai-Hulud / IronWorm VS Code Campaign
findings.affected_technology: JetBrains plugin marketplace serving IntelliJ IDEA / PyCharm / WebStorm / Rider / GoLand / CLion / Android Studio (JetBrains-derived) and other JetBrains IDEs. BleepingComputer 2026-06-16 (Lawrence Abrams) reports at least 15 malicious plugins published to the marketplace whose purpose is to extract AI API keys (Anthropic / OpenAI / Google / Cohere / Mistral / vendor-issued) from developer environments. Plugins masqueraded as legitimate productivity / AI-assistant integrations. Exfiltrated keys are directly monetisable (paid-tier model access for resale / proxy-as-a-service abuse), and many orgs grant the same keys access to internal proprietary data via embeddings / RAG endpoints — a credential compromise becomes a data-exfiltration foothold. Second 2026 AI-credential-theft cluster targeting developer-IDE marketplace surfaces after Mini Shai-Hulud / IronWorm VS Code + Claude Code config-persistence campaign (Watchtower 2026-05-21, 2026-06-06). Marketplace plugins as covert AI-key-collection channel warrants separate tracking from the broader supply-chain-worm cluster. IOC list pending from JetBrains.
findings.summary: JetBrains Marketplace ≥15 malicious plugins designed to steal Anthropic / OpenAI / Google / Cohere AI API keys from developer IDEs (BC 2026-06-16) — masqueraded as productivity / AI integrations; rotate every AI provider key resident in JetBrains workstations since 2026-05-01, default to 'trusted publishers only' plugin policy, prefer workload-identity over API-key access where supported.

findings.title: Cacti ≤ 1.2.30 CVE-2026-39949 — Authenticated OS Command Injection RCE Via host_notes Variable Substitution Into RRDtool Arguments; Public PoC On GitHub 2026-06-17
findings.affected_technology: Cacti network-monitoring platform ≤ 1.2.30. User-controlled host-metadata fields (specifically the device notes field) are substituted unsanitised into RRDtool command-line arguments via Cacti's variable replacement engine. Attack path: authenticated user with device + graph-template creation privileges injects shell metacharacters into the device-notes field, creates a graph template referencing |host_notes|, triggers graph rendering — rendering pipeline executes injected metacharacters as the web-server user (typically www-data / apache). Public PoC repository lukehebe/CVE-2026-39949 surfaced on GitHub 2026-06-17 supporting direct command execution (--cmd 'id') and out-of-band exfiltration (--oob your.oastify.com). Authentication required, lowering the immediate ceiling — but default-admin / weak-admin credentials are common on mid-tier Cacti deployments and credential-stuffing against Cacti is an established mass-exploitation route (continuing 2024 history). Vendor patch status: not yet confirmed at report time — track Cacti GitHub for fix-version.
findings.summary: Cacti ≤ 1.2.30 CVE-2026-39949 authenticated RCE via host_notes variable substitution into RRDtool command-line arguments; public PoC dropped on GitHub 2026-06-17 with --cmd and OOB modes; no vendor fix confirmed yet — inventory Cacti versions, rotate weak admin creds, restrict to management VLAN, hunt RRDtool args for shell metacharacters.

findings.title: Altium Enterprise Server Triple-CVE Batch — CVE-2026-11414 (CVSS 9.8) Hard-Coded Crypto Key Signing Vault Download URLs + CVE-2026-11420 (CVSS 9.8) Pre-Auth Path Traversal Arbitrary File Write In Network Installation Service + CVE-2026-11419 (CVSS 8.8) Authenticated Path Traversal In UploadController
findings.affected_technology: Altium Enterprise Server (centralised PCB / electronics-design vault platform used by manufacturers). NVD 2026-06-16 published a three-CVE batch: (1) CVE-2026-11414 (CVSS 9.8) — Vault service signs file-download URLs with a hard-coded cryptographic key, any party in possession of the binary can mint download URLs for arbitrary files served by the Vault. (2) CVE-2026-11420 (CVSS 9.8) — path traversal in Network Installation Service permits unauthenticated arbitrary file write + package archive read, the typical setup for installer-replacement-class compromise. (3) CVE-2026-11419 (CVSS 8.8) — path traversal in UploadController via inadequate validation of user-controlled path components in image uploads. Compromise yields source IP for PCB designs + access to the build/install distribution path to downstream developer workstations. Vendor patch published with the advisory; confirm patched build line via Altium PSIRT.
findings.summary: Altium Enterprise Server NVD 2026-06-16 triple-CVE batch — CVE-2026-11414 (CVSS 9.8) Vault hard-coded URL-signing key + CVE-2026-11420 (CVSS 9.8) pre-auth path-traversal arbitrary file write in Network Installation Service + CVE-2026-11419 (CVSS 8.8) authenticated path traversal in UploadController; patch published, restrict Vault + Network Installation Service to engineering jump host, audit downstream installer-package integrity out-of-band.

findings.title: UNK_Deadrop (North-Korea-Aligned) Developer Supply-Chain Campaign Hits ~100 Orgs Via Fake GitHub Recruitment Lures Delivering Cross-Platform 'Overlord' Loader Framework (macOS arm64 + Linux + Windows)
findings.affected_technology: Software-engineering / developer workstation attack surface across macOS arm64, Linux, and Windows. TheHackerNews 2026-06-16 reports a North-Korea-aligned cluster — UNK_Deadrop — running a developer-targeted social-engineering supply-chain campaign that has compromised an estimated ~100 organisations to date. Initial-access lure: fake GitHub recruitment messages ('please review this take-home project / code-review challenge') that route the candidate to a project repository whose build path drops a cross-platform 'Overlord' framework loader with macOS, Linux, and Windows payloads. Lure family closely matches 2024–2025 Lazarus 'Contagious Interview' pattern but Overlord is a new C2 + loader codebase, not BeaverTail / InvisibleFerret reuse. Notable: macOS variant ships native arm64 macOS persistence — among the first DPRK loaders with that capability, indicating substantial dev resources. For Watchtower scope: anyone in recruiting-adjacent or engineering roles approached by unsolicited GitHub recruiters in the last 60 days needs review; currently the highest-yield delivery vector against software-engineering targets.
findings.summary: UNK_Deadrop DPRK-aligned developer supply-chain campaign — ~100 orgs hit via fake GitHub recruitment 'take-home challenge' lures dropping cross-platform 'Overlord' loader (macOS arm64 + Linux + Windows) (THN 2026-06-16); new C2/loader codebase, not BeaverTail reuse; brief recruiting + engineering teams, sandbox unknown projects in disposable VMs, FIDO2-bind GitHub + cloud SSO.

findings.title: DragonForce Ransomware Deploys 'Backdoor.Turn' That Conceals C2 Traffic Inside Microsoft Teams Relay Infrastructure — Detection-Engineering Problem, Not A Teams Vulnerability
findings.affected_technology: Microsoft Teams (used as covert C2 carrier — not a vulnerability in Teams itself). BleepingComputer 2026-06-16 (Bill Toulas) reports the DragonForce ransomware affiliate program has deployed a custom backdoor 'Backdoor.Turn' that conceals command-and-control communications within Microsoft Teams relay infrastructure — C2 traffic encoded to traverse Teams media-relay control plane, indistinguishable from legitimate Teams telemetry to perimeter inspection. Same family as prior Slack-as-C2 and Discord-as-C2 abuse but materially harder to filter: Teams traffic is universally allowed out of corporate networks, uses TLS-pinned endpoints that conventional decryption breaks, and the volume is high enough to hide low-rate C2 cadence inside. Detection-engineering problem: behavioural detection on Teams media-relay flow shape (volume + cadence + destination distribution) against per-user baselines, not perimeter-block.
findings.summary: DragonForce ransomware 'Backdoor.Turn' hides C2 inside Microsoft Teams media-relay infrastructure (BC 2026-06-16) — TTP, not a Teams CVE; conventional decryption breaks against TLS-pinned Teams endpoints; onboard Teams flow shape into SIEM with baseline + drift detection, hunt for non-Teams.exe processes initiating outbound to Teams relay endpoints.
